serviceCards.title: Wood & Privacy Fence Installation
serviceCards.desc: Replacing a worn 6-foot fence or stepping up to board-on-board with cedar pickets and steel posts. One DFW firm advertises installed cedar privacy fence at $18 to $28 per linear foot, while another advertises $30 to $60 for a 6-foot wood fence, so prices vary widely.

serviceCards.title: Fence Repair
serviceCards.desc: Leaning posts, missing pickets and storm-damaged sections. One Dallas firm advertises a single post reset with new concrete at $150 to $400 and board replacement at $25 to $60 per board.

serviceCards.title: Gate Repair & Automatic Gates
serviceCards.desc: Sagging walk gates, worn hinges, dead openers and sliding tracks. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license.

serviceCards.title: Wrought Iron & Ornamental Fences
serviceCards.desc: Iron or steel pickets for a front yard or a side-yard run. One Dallas-area firm advertises residential tubular steel fence at $30 to $45 per linear foot installed.

processSteps.title: Call or email and describe the fence
processSteps.desc: Tell us what you have: a leaning wood fence, a storm gap, a dead gate opener or a new 8-foot board-on-board run. Mention your HOA and whether a dog is loose in the yard.

processSteps.title: An independent contractor scopes the job
processSteps.desc: The contractor will want the linear feet, the height, the material and any gates, and may look at the site, including alley access and corner-lot sight lines. Texas811 says that when you hire a contractor, calling 811 before digging is the contractor's job.

processSteps.title: Compare written quotes
processSteps.desc: You get a written quote from the contractor. Get two or three, check that each lists the same height, posts, pickets and gate hardware, and ask each about city registration and proof of insurance.

faq.q: How does fence pricing and scoping work in Dallas?
faq.a: A contractor prices a fence from the linear feet, the height, the material, the post type, the style and any gates, so two quotes only compare if those match. For wood, one DFW firm advertises installed cedar privacy fence at $18 to $28 per linear foot, another advertises $30 to $60 for a 6-foot wood fence, and a third advertises $20 to $36 for board-on-board, so published ranges overlap and contradict each other. Height changes the total sharply: a national guide (Fixr, 2025) puts 150 feet at $2,250 to $6,000 for a 6-foot fence and $4,500 to $12,750 for 8 feet. None of these are quotes from this site, and a contractor will give you the number in writing.

faq.q: How fast will someone respond, and how long does a fence job take?
faq.a: This site cannot promise a callback time or an install date, because the work is done by independent contractors and their schedules change with the season and after storms. Call now, say if it is urgent, such as a fence down with a dog in the yard or a gate stuck open, and ask each contractor to put a start date and a finish estimate in the written quote. A contractor who will not write a date down is worth a second look.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Dallas?
faq.a: The City of Dallas fence permit checklist (form 26-001) says a permit is required for fences over 4 feet in a front yard or over 6 feet in all other locations, and that the maximum allowable height is 9 feet. Historic and conservation districts and floodplain areas can add approvals. The City's application guide also says fence applications require a general contractor to be listed. Confirm the details with the City at (214) 948-4480 and with your HOA before you build.

faq.q: Can my HOA stop me from building the fence I want?
faq.a: Often it can control the type of fence. Texas Property Code Section 202.023 limits an HOA's ability to ban a perimeter fence outright, but it still lets the association regulate fence type and, for example, require a driveway gate to sit at least 10 feet back from the right-of-way on certain roads. Get approval in writing before the contractor orders materials.

faq.q: Who pays for a fence shared with my neighbor?
faq.a: Texas does not appear to have a statute that sets a split for a residential boundary fence. Texas Law Help says that if both neighbors use a fence straddling the property line, both own it and would share the cost of repairing and replacing it, while a fence entirely on one lot belongs to that owner. This is general information, not legal advice, so talk to your neighbor early and put any agreement in writing.

faq.q: Is White Rock Fence Co the fence contractor?
faq.a: No. White Rock Fence Co is advertising for independent Dallas-area fence contractors and does not build, repair or install fences or gates. Texas has no state license for fence contractors, though some cities, including Dallas, Richardson and Irving, register them. Ask whoever quotes your job for their city registration and proof of insurance.
